html:
Solomon's Temple, the First Temple, was the temple in Jerusalem that, according to the Hebrew Bible, King Solomon built in the 10th century BCE on the hill now called the Temple Mount. No remains of it have been securely identified, and its date rests on the Bible.

The Bible describes a stone building lined with cedar from Lebanon and gold, built with the help of Hiram, king of Tyre. Its innermost room held the Ark of the Covenant. It was the centre of the worship of the God of Israel and Judah, and kings of Judah made it the only place for sacrifice.

It was destroyed by Babylon in 587 or 586 BCE. The Second Temple was built on the site after the exile. Jews still mourn both temples on the fast of Tisha B'Av. See also Judaism.
